title: Capacity-probing regional steering: graduated latency & geo-pinning policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a capacity-probing regional steering policy that combines latency-based routing, geo-pinning for data residency, and capacity-aware scoring. The policy should gracefully fail over across regions using circuit-breaker semantics and implement load-shedding tiers for overloaded regions. This ticket covers algorithm design, simulation harness, API flags, and an initial gradual rollout plan.
background: Previous routing work covered static geo routing and simple latency steering. We observed two operational gaps: (1) tail latency spikes when a region becomes transiently overloaded despite healthy average latency, and (2) suboptimal failovers that either overload the next region or violate customer geo-pinning requirements. This effort unifies steering logic with active capacity probing and circuit breakers so the router can make resilient, SLO-aware decisions.
decision_log: 2026-02-18: Chosen hybrid approach combining exponential weighted latency score with a capacity score derived from per-Pool telemetry. 2026-02-22: Use soft geo-pinning with strict exceptions for regulated accounts: default is prefer-local then global; regulated accounts set geo_pin=strict. 2026-02-25: Circuit breaker thresholds: open when error_rate>2% OR sustained 95th percentile infra latency > 2x SLO for 3m. 2026-02-28: Load-shedding priority order approved: 1) non-authenticated low-priority batching, 2) degrade to smaller model, 3) surface 429 with retry-after when above 95th capacity.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Router exposes new policy 'capacity-probing' behind feature-flag. 2) Simulation shows less than 10% additional cross-region failure during synthetic 2x load spikes compared to baseline. 3) Regulated accounts with geo_pin=strict never route to non-compliant region. 4) Circuit breaker trips and recovers per documented thresholds in simulation. 5) Rollout plan validated in canary with <1% error delta and observability dashboards present.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged deploy to canary (10% of traffic) for non-regulated tenants for 48h. Phase 1: Canary for regulated tenants with geo_pin=prefer for 24h; monitor. Phase 2: Region-specific canaries: enable capacity-probing in eu-west-1 only with synthetic traffic injection. Phase 3: Gradual ramp every 12h + SLO guardrails. Revert if circuit-breaker open rate exceeds 0.5% sustained or customer errors increase by >2x.
monitoring_and_alerting: Expose metrics: region_capacity_score (0-1), region_latency_p50/p95/p99, region_error_rate, region_queue_depth, circuit_breaker_state, shed_count_by_tier. Alerts: A1 region_capacity_score < 0.45 for >2m; A2 circuit_breaker_state=open for >1m; A3 shed_count_by_tier > 1% of requests in 5m. Dashboards: per-tenant and per-region steering heatmap, failover timeline, backing infra metrics (GPU util, queue length).
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic. Integration tests using routing simulator with 3-region topology (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1). Chaos tests: abrupt region CPU saturation, network partitions, delayed KV cache responses. Canary tests include golden traffic replay and synthetic tail-latency spike injection. Performance regression test: ensure routing decision adds <1ms median overhead.
implementation_notes: Capacity score formula (initial): capacity_score = sigmoid(0.6 * (1 - gpu_util) + 0.3 * (1 - normalized_queue) + 0.1 * (1 - recent_error_rate)). Latency score computed via ewma on p99 normalized to SLO. Final steering weight = w_lat*latency_score + w_cap*capacity_score - geo_penalty where w_lat=0.55, w_cap=0.35. Geo-pin adds +0.25 bonus to local region when prefer; strict forces region inclusion. The router will actively probe candidate regions with lightweight 1-5 token synthetic requests when capacity_score falls into a 'gray' zone [0.4,0.65] to avoid mass failovers.
playbook: When alerts fire: 1) Check region_capacity_score and circuit_breaker_state. 2) If breaker open, inspect recent error types (OOM, timeouts). 3) If due to resource saturation, scale Dedicated pools if available or enable temporary shedding for non-critical tenants. 4) For false positives from telemetry, flip feature-flag to previous routing. 5) Post-incident: run root-cause and update thresholds.
open_questions_and_risks: How to weigh cold-start model compilation delay in capacity_score for new model variants? Risk: probing could increase load on overloaded region if not rate-limited. Need to ensure telemetries are low-latency (<10s) to avoid stale steering. Operational complexity: rollout coordination with Dedicated capacity teams.
notes: Link PR for prototype scoring service: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1458. Prototype simulation notebooks: drive.google.com/drive/fake-sim/steering-sim.ipynb. Related RFC: confluence.redwood.ai/rfc/multi-region-steering-2026.
